senses.definition: A match or close match between sounds at the ends of words.
senses.example: Bat and hat make a rhyme.

senses.definition: A pattern of sounds, beats, or movements as they happen in time.
senses.example: We clapped the rhythm of the tune without singing it.

senses.definition: One of the curved bones that form part of the chest and help protect the organs inside.
senses.example: We counted the ribs on the skeleton model.

senses.definition: A raised strip or support shaped a little like a curved bone.
senses.example: The umbrella’s ribs held its cloth open.

senses.definition: Curved bones and nearby cartilage that surround the chest and protect parts inside it.
senses.example: My rib cage moves when I take a deep breath.

senses.definition: A long, narrow strip of material used to tie or decorate things.
senses.example: She tied a blue ribbon around the box.

senses.definition: Small grains from a plant, cooked and eaten as food, or the plant that grows them.
senses.example: We served rice with the vegetables.

senses.definition: Having plenty of money or other valuable things.
senses.example: In the story, a rich traveler bought the whole inn.

senses.definition: Having a great deal of something useful or pleasing.
senses.example: The soil is rich in materials that help plants grow.

senses.definition: Strong and full in taste, color, or sound.
senses.example: The soup had a rich tomato flavor.

senses.definition: A question or puzzle that gives clues and asks you to figure out a tricky answer.
senses.example: The riddle made me think about a different meaning of the word key.

senses.definition: To travel on or in a vehicle or on the back of an animal.
senses.example: I rode my bike around the block.

senses.definition: A trip on a vehicle, animal, or amusement machine.
senses.example: We went for a ride on the merry-go-round.

senses.definition: To stay through something difficult until it passes.
senses.example: We rode out the storm together inside the cabin.

senses.definition: A long raised part of the land or another surface.
senses.example: A narrow ridge ran along the top of the hill.

senses.definition: So silly or hard to believe that it may make people laugh.
senses.example: It was a ridiculous sight when the dog ran by in three socks.

senses.definition: Correct or suitable for what is needed.
senses.example: She found the right answer by counting the groups.

senses.definition: The side that is opposite the left.
senses.example: Turn to the right after the bridge.

senses.definition: Something that people are allowed to do or are entitled to have under a rule or law.
senses.example: We learned about the right to vote.

senses.definition: To set something upright again after it has tipped or fallen over.
senses.example: We helped right the empty flowerpot after it fell.

senses.definition: An angle that makes a square corner and measures ninety degrees.
senses.example: The sides of a sheet of paper meet at a right angle.

senses.definition: As soon as possible or with no delay.
senses.example: The bell rang and we went to the door right away.

senses.definition: The edge around a round object or opening.
senses.example: A drop ran down the rim of the glass.

senses.definition: A small band worn around a finger.
senses.example: The ring was too big for my thumb.

senses.definition: A circle of things around a space.
senses.example: We made a ring of chairs for the game.

senses.definition: To make a clear sound like a bell, or cause that sound.
senses.example: I heard the school bell ring from the playground.

senses.definition: To wash something briefly with clean water to remove soap or dirt.
senses.example: I rinsed the bowl after scrubbing it.

senses.definition: To tear something apart, often quickly.
senses.example: Be careful not to rip the thin paper.

senses.definition: A tear in cloth, paper, or another material.
senses.example: I found a rip in the knee of my jeans.

senses.definition: A strip of plants between a stream or other waterway and land next to it.
senses.example: The riparian buffer shaded the creek and held the bank together.

senses.definition: Fully grown and ready to pick or eat, said of fruit and some other foods.
senses.example: We picked the ripe peaches before dinner.

senses.definition: A little wave or series of waves on a surface.
senses.example: A pebble made ripples across the pond.

senses.definition: To form or move in small waves.
senses.example: The flag rippled as the breeze got stronger.

senses.definition: To move upward or get higher.
senses.example: We watched the balloon rise above the trees.

senses.definition: To get up from lying or sitting.
senses.example: Please rise from your seat when it is your turn.

senses.definition: An increase in an amount or level.
senses.example: A rise in the river level covered our stepping stones.

senses.definition: A chance that something bad or unwanted might happen.
senses.example: Wearing shoes with good grip lowers the risk of slipping.

senses.definition: To do something even though you might lose something or face a problem.
senses.example: I stayed on the path so I would not risk getting lost.

senses.definition: A person or group competing for the same goal or prize.
senses.example: Our closest rival won its match, too.

senses.definition: To be as good, strong, or impressive as someone or something else.
senses.example: The park’s autumn colors rival those in the hills.

senses.definition: A wide path or prepared surface used for traveling, especially by vehicles.
senses.example: The road curved gently around the pond.

senses.definition: To make a deep, powerful sound.
senses.example: The crowd began to roar after the final goal.

senses.definition: A deep, powerful sound.
senses.example: We heard the roar of water below the bridge.

senses.definition: To cook with dry heat, often in an oven or near a fire.
senses.example: We like to roast carrots until their edges turn brown.

senses.definition: A large piece of meat cooked with dry heat, often in an oven.
senses.example: Dad sliced the roast before everyone sat down.

senses.definition: To take something from a person or place by stealing, often using force or threats.
senses.example: In the mystery, thieves tried to rob the jewelry shop.

senses.definition: A machine made to do tasks automatically, often by following coded instructions or signals from a controller.
senses.example: Our robot followed a black line taped to the floor.

senses.definition: A natural solid material made of one or more minerals or other solid substances.
senses.example: We saw three different colors in the rock.

senses.definition: To move gently back and forth or from side to side.
senses.example: The small boat began to rock when a wave went past.

senses.definition: A kind of popular music often played with a strong beat, guitars, and drums.
senses.example: The drummer plays in a rock band.

senses.definition: A cell near the back of the eye that responds well to weak light.
senses.example: Rod cells help me see the ground in very dim light.

senses.definition: A part a person plays in a story, performance, or group activity.
senses.example: I played the role of the guide in our class play.

senses.definition: The usual job or purpose of someone or something in a larger process.
senses.example: Earthworms play a role in breaking up and mixing soil.

senses.definition: To move by turning over and over.
senses.example: The ball began to roll down the hill.

senses.definition: To curl or wrap something into a tube, ball, or bundle.
senses.example: We will roll the poster before putting it in the tube.

senses.definition: A small loaf of bread for one person.
senses.example: My soup came with a warm roll.

senses.definition: Something wrapped around itself or a center in layers.
senses.example: There was one roll of tape left.

senses.definition: The outside covering at the top of a building or vehicle.
senses.example: Rain drummed on the roof of the bus.

senses.definition: A channel that catches rain running off an edge of a roof and guides it toward a drain or pipe.
senses.example: The roof gutter caught water that slid down the shingles.

senses.definition: A part of a building set off by walls, usually with a door.
senses.example: The game room was beside the kitchen.

senses.definition: Free space for someone or something to fit.
senses.example: There is room for one more map in my bag.

senses.definition: A place where a bird or some other animals rest or sleep.
senses.example: At dusk the turkey flew up to its roost.

senses.definition: A part of a plant, often underground, that helps hold it in place and take in water and other materials.
senses.example: The bean’s long white root grew to the bottom of the cup.

senses.definition: The basic part or earliest form of a thing, such as a word.
senses.example: The root of replay and playful is play.

senses.definition: To give support and cheer for someone, usually followed by for.
senses.example: We will root for our friends in the relay.

senses.definition: A thick, strong cord made by twisting or weaving strands together.
senses.example: We lowered the bucket on a rope.

senses.definition: A plant that usually has prickles and showy flowers, or the flower of that plant.
senses.example: A pink rose grew beside the front steps.

senses.definition: Past form of rise, meaning went upward, increased, or got up.
senses.example: The balloon rose above the trees.

senses.definition: To break down and decay, often as bacteria or fungi grow on something that was once alive.
senses.example: The fallen apple began to rot in the wet grass.

senses.definition: Decay in food, wood, or other things that were once alive.
senses.example: A soft part of the log showed signs of rot.

senses.definition: The turning of something around a center or an axis. The word can also mean one whole turn.
senses.example: Earth’s rotation gives us day and night.

senses.definition: An order in which people or things take turns so each has a chance.
senses.example: The coach wrote down the rotation for each position.

senses.definition: A machine part that spins, such as the blades on top of a helicopter.
senses.example: The helicopter’s rotor pushed air downward.

senses.definition: Uneven and not smooth when you touch it.
senses.example: The rough stone scratched my glove.

senses.definition: Difficult, harsh, or full of problems.
senses.example: We had a rough trip when the bus broke down.

senses.definition: Made quickly, without careful finishing or exact detail.
senses.example: I made a rough drawing before using the good paper.

senses.definition: Shaped like a circle, ball, or smooth curve.
senses.example: We traced the round bottom of a cup.

senses.definition: One complete turn, stage, or set of turns in an activity.
senses.example: After one round of the game, we switched teams.

senses.definition: To go around a corner or bend.
senses.example: We rounded the last bend and saw the finish line.

senses.definition: To change a number to the nearest or chosen place value under a rule.
senses.example: If you round forty-eight to the nearest ten, you get fifty.

senses.definition: Changing a number to a nearby, simpler number, such as the closest ten.
senses.example: Rounding 48 to the nearest ten gives 50.

senses.definition: The way someone or something goes from one place to another.
senses.example: The map shows a shorter route to the lake.

senses.definition: To send someone or something along a chosen path.
senses.example: They will route the buses around the bridge while it is closed.

senses.definition: A device or program that passes packets toward other computer networks.
senses.example: A router can send a message from our home network toward the internet.

senses.definition: A straight line of people or things side by side.
senses.example: I put the cups in a row along the shelf.

senses.definition: To move a boat using oars.
senses.example: We took turns learning to row the boat.

senses.definition: A loud or angry argument.
senses.example: The neighbors had a row about a fence between their yards.

senses.definition: Connected with a king, queen, or their family.
senses.example: The royal family arrived at the station by train.

senses.definition: To move something back and forth across a surface while pressing on it.
senses.example: Rub the paper gently with the side of your crayon.

senses.definition: An act of moving something across a surface while pressing.
senses.example: The old spot came off after a quick rub with a damp cloth.

senses.definition: A tough material that can bend or stretch and is used for things such as tires and erasers.
senses.example: The ball bounced because it was made of rubber.

senses.definition: A movable part that helps turn the nose of a boat or an aircraft from side to side.
senses.example: The rudder can swing one way or the other at the back of the plane’s tail.

senses.definition: Not showing care for other people’s feelings or good manners.
senses.example: It was rude to talk over the person reading aloud.

senses.definition: A thick piece of fabric that covers part of a floor.
senses.example: We sat on the rug while the story was read.

senses.definition: To spoil or damage something so badly it cannot be used or enjoyed as planned.
senses.example: Leaving the book in the rain could ruin it.

senses.definition: A part of an old building that remains after most of it has fallen or been torn down, often called ruins.
senses.example: We saw stone walls among the castle ruins.

senses.definition: A direction that says what someone must or must not do in a place, game, or situation.
senses.example: Our game has one rule about taking turns.

senses.definition: To govern or have power over a country or group.
senses.example: In the story, three sisters rule the island together.

senses.definition: To make an official decision about something.
senses.example: The referee can rule that the ball went out of bounds.

senses.definition: To decide that something cannot be the answer or is no longer a choice.
senses.example: I can rule out the square piece because the opening is round.

senses.definition: A straight strip with marks for measuring and a straight edge for drawing lines.
senses.example: My ruler showed that the leaf was five inches long.

senses.definition: A person who governs a country or people.
senses.example: The ruler sent an invitation to leaders from nearby lands.

senses.definition: A low, steady or rolling sound.
senses.example: We heard a rumble of thunder in the distance.

senses.definition: To make or move with a low, rolling sound.
senses.example: The trucks rumbled across the bridge.

senses.definition: A story people pass around without knowing whether it is true.
senses.example: I heard a rumor that the picnic might move indoors.

senses.definition: To move quickly on foot, taking quicker steps than when walking.
senses.example: I ran to the big tree and back.

senses.definition: To operate a machine or continue working.
senses.example: The fan can run all afternoon.

senses.definition: To manage the work of a group, activity, or place.
senses.example: The student council helped run the book fair.

senses.definition: An outing or exercise in which someone moves quickly on foot.
senses.example: We went for a run before breakfast.

senses.definition: To use everything you had of something, so none is left.
senses.example: If we run out of paper, we can use the other side of our sketches.

senses.definition: A stem that creeps away from a parent plant and can make new plants along the way.
senses.example: The strawberry’s runner reached over the edge of the pot.

senses.definition: A way to lay bricks in rows so the end of a brick sits over part of a brick below it instead of above another end.
senses.example: The running bond made a repeating pattern on the school wall.

senses.definition: Water that flows off land or buildings instead of staying where it fell or soaking into the ground.
senses.example: Runoff followed the edge of the road into a drain.

senses.definition: In or connected with the countryside instead of a city or large town.
senses.example: We passed barns and fields along the rural road.

senses.definition: To move or act in a hurry.
senses.example: We did not need to rush because the bus was late.

senses.definition: A sudden movement, feeling, or period of activity.
senses.example: There was a rush of cold air when we opened the door.

senses.definition: The reddish-brown material that can form when iron or steel reacts with oxygen in the presence of moisture.
senses.example: There was rust on the old gate after years in the rain.

senses.definition: To develop rust.
senses.example: A steel tool can rust if it stays wet.
